us-maria-cantwell.text: Today is Social Security’s 91st birthday, a lifeline benefit that keeps nearly 300,000 Washingtonians above the poverty line. In the Senate, I will continue to protect the Social Security program.

Yesterday we learned from Tom Clemo of California Interagency Incident Management Team 7, Maj. Gen. Gent Welsh of the Washington National Guard, and local fire chiefs that the Spokane fires could have been a lot worse. (1/3)

Today in Yakima we celebrated the grand opening of Casa de la Mora, a housing complex for people with disabilities, young adults exiting homelessness or foster care, and low-income households. This is the transformative element that might get somebody from just existing to thriving again.

Today is Purple Heart Day, when we remember the bravery and sacrifices of Americans who were wounded or lost their lives in service of our nation. They have helped safeguard the United States and all it stands for.

Today Interior Sec. Burgum, Agriculture Sec. Rollins, DOI Wildland Fire Service Director Brian Fennessy, and USFS officials briefed Senators on keeping assets in the Northwest as we are at a Preparedness Level 5, an extreme wildfire designation. (1/4)
Today is Primary Election Day in WA! Voters, be sure to return your ballot to a state ballot drop box or your local voting center by 8:00 PM PT TONIGHT. (1/2)

Today is the 6th anniversary of our successful fight to pass the Great American Outdoors Act. This law fully funded the Land and Water Conservation Fund, which has invested over $730 million in conserving open space and public lands in Washington since its creation.

Today I joined the entire WA congressional delegation in a letter to President Trump supporting an expedited Emergency Declaration for counties and tribes affected by the large, fast-moving wildfires across our state.
The Spokane fire is the top fire in our nation. The federal government is going to give us the resources we need here on the ground. (1/2)

I am monitoring the dangerous fires in Spokane and across Central Washington. My office and I are in contact with local, state, and federal agencies to help make sure firefighters and first responders have the resources they need. (1/2)

us-amy-klobuchar.text: As I go around our state, to all of Minnesota’s 87 counties, I hear the same thing: health care costs are putting too much pressure on families, small businesses, and communities. We can do better.

I was in Cloquet today at Community Memorial Hospital to talk about my plan to make health care more affordable and accessible – and to strengthen the community hospitals that are there for Minnesotans when they need them most.

A great afternoon at the LiUNA Minnesota picnic yesterday! It was wonderful to see union members coming together to support their neighbors, help families in need, and give back to their community. 

Proud to have their endorsement and excited for what we can accomplish together.
The disrespect is appalling. Our men and women in uniform deserve so much better.

Every year, the India Association of Minnesota gathers in St. Paul to celebrate the anniversary of India’s independence – and I was honored to join leaders of the Indian American community for this celebration.

Health insurance premiums for people on the individual market are skyrocketing because the Trump administration let the federal tax credits expire. My priority as Governor will be to reduce premiums and lower health care costs, so families can afford to get the care they need.

Thinking of the members & families of 103D ESC Unit as they gather in Des Moines to honor those they lost, including Minnesota’s own Nicole Amor. We hold the 103D & their family and friends & Joey & his & Nicole’s kids in our prayers today. 🙏
Great joining LiUNA Minnesota members and their families today in Como Park! I’m grateful to have their support, and proud to stand with the workers who are building Minnesota’s future.
Honored to attend Indiafest today—an incredible celebration of Indian culture, entrepreneurship and the invaluable contributions our 50,000-plus Indian-American community makes to our state.

My opponent calls Trump’s health care cuts “good for Minnesota.” And when Trump refused to extend the premium tax credits, she stood by and did nothing.

As Governor, I’ll take action to bring down prescription drug costs and give Minnesotans relief from rising premiums.
